question.value: What is the gas temperature structure of the young disk-like structure around the Class 0 protostar IRAS 16293-2422A, as probed by H2CS line ratios?

evidence.quote: We set out to determine the gas temperature of the young disk-like structure around the Class 0 protostar IRAS 16293–2422A.
covering frequencies between 329.147 and 362.896 GHz in Band 7 (project-id: 2013.1.00278.S)
(0.5$\ensuremath{''}$; project-id: 2012.1.00712.S)
IRAS 16293 was also observed at 0.5$\ensuremath{''}$ resolution by program 2016.1.01150.S (PI: Taquet).
The PILS program also contains eight selected windows in Band 6 ($\sim$230 GHz)

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: Band 7 resolution 0.2 km/s (244 kHz); Band 6 and 2016 data 0.15 km/s (122 kHz)

evidence.quote: The data have a spectral resolution of 0.2 km s$^{-1}$ (244 kHz)
a restoring beam of 0.5$\ensuremath{''}$ ($\sim$70 AU)
a sensitivity of 7–10 mJy beam$^{-1}$ channel$^{-1}$, or $\sim$5 mJy beam$^{-1}$ km s$^{-1}$ across the entire frequency range
which contains collisional rate coefficients for H$_2$CS from (cite: Wiesenfeld2013))
The transition frequencies and other line data were taken from the CDMS database (cite: Muller2001; Muller2005).

what.value: H2CS column density toward IRAS 16293B of 1.3e15 cm-2

evidence.quote: Toward IRAS 16293B, a H$_2$CS column density of $1.3 \times 10^{15}$ cm$^{-2}$ was found (cite: Drozdovskaya2018).
A detailed description of the data reduction and continuum subtraction can be found in (cite: Jorgensen2016).

what.value: Data reduction and continuum subtraction of PILS Band 7 and Band 6 data

evidence.quote: The data reduction proceeded in the same manner as the Band 7 data (cite: Jorgensen2016).
The data reduction is described in (cite: Taquet2018).

what.value: Line isolation via methanol peak-velocity map and VINE maps

evidence.quote: we make use of the method outlined in (cite: Calcutt2018) to isolate the formaldehyde and thioformaldehyde lines

unstated_but_needed: Imaging parameters (robust, cell, image size, deconvolver)
Whether Band 6/7 images were smoothed to a common beam
Exact RADEX grid ranges and the LTE calculation details

analysis_steps.goal: Isolate lines and build velocity-corrected maps

method.value: Peak velocity per pixel from bright methanol line used to identify target lines; VINE moment-0 maps

evidence.quote: the peak velocity in each pixel is determined using a bright methanol transition (7$_{3,5}$ – 6$_{4,4}$ at 337.519 GHz)

method.value: Moment 8 (peak flux per pixel); pixels with too much blending excluded

evidence.quote: we extract the peak flux per pixel in order to make spatial maps of the line ratios and hence temperature structure

analysis_steps.goal: Convert H2CS line ratios to temperature

method.value: Grid of RADEX non-LTE models; LTE where no collision rates

evidence.quote: converted into temperature maps using a grid of RADEX non-LTE radiative transfer models

key_parameters.value: n(H2)=1e10 cm-3, N(H2CS)=1e14 cm-2, line width 2 km/s

evidence.quote: A column density of $10^{14}$ cm$^{-2}$ is adopted in the temperature calculations.

assumptions.value: Densities >1e7 cm-3 make ratios density independent

evidence.quote: the exact value adopted for the density does not influence the derived temperatures and we use a value of $10^{10}$ cm$^{-3}$

validation.value: Error bars from image rms propagated through RADEX; compared with LTE results

evidence.quote: Error bars on the line ratios are calculated from the image rms, and converted into error bars on the temperature using the RADEX calculations

analysis_steps.goal: Rotation diagrams per pixel as cross-check

method.value: Rotation diagrams for every pixel in 2"x2" region; fits to all, para, ortho, or Eup<200 K lines

evidence.quote: rotation diagrams are made for every pixel in a $2^{\prime\prime} \times 2^{\prime\prime}$ region surrounding the continuum position

assumptions.value: Ortho-to-para ratio 2 (1-3 changes T by <~30 K)

evidence.quote: An ortho-to-para ratio of 2 is assumed, but varying this between 1 and 3 changes the derived temperature by $\lesssim$30 K.

used_for.value: Non-LTE radiative transfer grid to convert line ratios to temperature

evidence.quote: a grid of RADEX non-LTE radiative transfer models (cite: vanderTak2007)
the temperature is between $\sim$100–175 K in the inner $\sim$150 AU, and drops to $\sim$75 K at $\sim$200 AU
drops to $\sim$75 K at $\sim$200 AU

results_numeric.value: ~60 at 200 AU rising to ~150 at center

evidence.quote: The first three cases result in temperatures of $\sim$60 K at 200 AU rising up to $\sim$150 at source center.
The non-LTE RADEX results give temperatures higher by $\sim$20–50 K than the LTE results

findings_qualitative.value: High-velocity wings of H2CS 7(0,7)-6(0,6) arise from line blending, not Keplerian rotation

evidence.quote: The large velocity gradient thus seems the result of line blending and not Keplerian rotation.

claims.hypothesis: Is the disk-like structure warm and does temperature rise steeply inside 100 AU as in envelope models?
claims.experiment: H2CS line ratios converted to temperature with RADEX, plus rotation diagrams
claims.result: 100-175 K within 150 AU, ~75 K at 200 AU, no steep rise at <100 AU
claims.finding: Consistent with envelope profiles down to ~100 AU but flatter inside

evidence.quote: does not follow the temperature rise seen in these profiles at smaller radii

claims.hypothesis: Is there a temperature jump at the disk-envelope interface?
claims.finding: No evidence for centrifugal-barrier heating at current resolution

evidence.quote: no jump is seen in the temperature at the disk-envelope interface

claims.hypothesis: Does IRAS 16293A's disk-like structure differ in temperature from L1527?

evidence.quote: The temperature in the disk-like structure around IRAS 16293A is $\sim$75 K higher than in the young Class 0/I disk L1527, on similar scales.

why_this_method.value: Ratios of H2CS lines across Ka ladders trace kinetic temperature independent of pointing, beam and calibration

evidence.quote: can provide a measure of the kinetic temperature unaffected by relative pointing uncertainties, beam-size differences and absolute calibration uncertainties

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: H2CO, H2(13)CO and D2CO rejected: too few unblended lines, optically thick, or continuum oversubtraction

evidence.quote: However, all these ratios are near unity, suggesting that the emission is optically thick

limitations_admitted.value: Line blending and limited 0.5" resolution; optically thin higher-resolution tracers are needed

evidence.quote: High resolution observations of optically thin lines are required to establish the details of the temperature profile in the inner $\sim$100 AU.

referee_caveats_inferred: Peak-flux ratios in the blended central pixels may be biased
Assumed column density of 1e14 cm-2 and single density are not fitted
Unresolved binary A1/A2 and dust optical depth not modeled
No formal temperature fitting or uncertainty budget beyond rms

data_public_as_stated.value: Data are ALMA programs with listed project codes; PILS is a public survey

evidence.quote: This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2012.1.00712.S, ADS/JAO.ALMA#2013.1.00278.S and ADS/JAO.ALMA#2016.1.01150.S.

missing_for_reproduction: Reduced PILS cubes details/imaging parameters (in Jorgensen2016)

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Hundreds of GB for the three programs' raw data; PILS reduced cubes tens of GB
reproducibility.score_reason: Methodology is clear and simple, but reduction/imaging is deferred to other papers and pixel selection is not specified.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Main numbers are approximate ranges and depend on unspecified blending-based pixel selection and inherited reductions.
